description: A timeline for the web: a custom element and a live instance over a DOM-free engine, drawn as SVG — items in lanes along an axis of time, to pan, zoom, select and edit by pointer, touch or keyboard.
scope: The timeline as the library draws it — the element, its views and tools, in the default configuration and with editing on — in Chromium, on the documentation's own pages. The page around it, its title, language, headings, links and help, is the host's.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.remarks: Every drawn item is an option named by its label, its dates and its lane; the axis, the lane bands and the repeated text are hidden from assistive technology, because the options already say it.

tests.test: makes every drawn item an option with a unique id, a name with its dates
hides everything that repeats or decorates what the items say

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio and no video.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio and no video.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio and no video.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio and no video.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio and no video.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.remarks: The timeline is a listbox of options, each with its place among all items (`aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`); nested groups are a tree; a Gantt task names its predecessors and successors.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.remarks: The keyboard and the accessible order walk the items by start, then by row, the same in every orientation and direction.

tests.test: orders by start, then row, and is built once per layout

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.remarks: The library gives no instructions; the words around a timeline are the host's.

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.remarks: Not locked to an orientation: below its breakpoint the timeline turns vertical, and follows a live resize without a reload.

tests.test: is horizontal at and above the breakpoint, vertical below it

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.remarks: The library collects no information about the user and draws no form field: the date prompt for `g` is the host's, opened from the `jumpRequest` event.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.remarks: Selection and focus are an outline ring, not a colour; an overbooked resource is banded and its items say so in their names.

tests.test: points at the keyboard's item, and rings it

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.remarks: The library plays no audio.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: Every text token against every surface it is drawn on is at least 4.5:1, in the light and the dark theme, computed as WCAG defines contrast.

tests.test: computes contrast as WCAG defines it

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.remarks: With the browser's zoom the timeline is laid out again for the narrower view and loses no item, name or key: tested at 200% (a 1280 × 800 window, 640 × 400 CSS pixels at two device pixels each) and at 400% (320 CSS pixels, see 1.4.10). Text-only enlargement does not reach it: its type sizes are pixels from the density, so a root font size of 200% and a 32-pixel default font in the browser leave its labels at 12 and its axis at 11 pixels while the page's own text grows to 64 (tested). A browser's text-only zoom, which enlarges pixel sizes too, is not tested.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.remarks: Item labels and tick labels are text — SVG text, or HTML in the item — in every theme and density; nothing is a picture of text.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.remarks: At 320 CSS pixels (a 1280-pixel window at 400%) the element turns vertical and dense, the page does not scroll sideways, every item keeps its whole name, and the keys bring each item wholly into view; at 256 pixels tall a horizontal timeline, given a height that fits, shows every lane, so nothing scrolls both ways. Two lanes take 336 pixels across in the dense layout, 16 more than 320: the lanes then scroll across inside the timeline (the keys do it for the focused item), as two-dimensional content may; the page itself never scrolls sideways. The timeline's height is the host's.

tests.test: an explicit orientation overrides the measurement

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.remarks: An item's outline, the focus ring, the selection outline, the major ticks and the loading mark are at least 3:1 against what they are drawn on, in both themes. In forced colours every shape takes the reader's system colours instead — surface and item fill `Canvas`, outlines and text `CanvasText`, minor lines `GrayText`, focus and selection `Highlight` at 3 pixels — tested in a light and a dark palette.

tests.test: paint in the reader's system colours, wider where selected

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.remarks: The element measures each label with the spacing it is drawn with — the reader's letter and word spacing, read off a drawn label — and measures and lays out again when that spacing comes or goes after load, with no resize or call: under WCAG's spacing (line height 1.5, letters 0.12em, words 0.16em, paragraphs 2em, all `!important`) every label of the element's test page keeps its whole text in a box that holds it, as without the spacing, also after it draws again at another size; the taller line stays centred in its box, nothing runs into the axis, the keys still work, and the item's accessible name keeps the whole label (tested on the element in its shadow root and on an instance in the page). Where the core's renderer is used directly, labels are measured with what the host passes as `measureText`, or, without one, with a font-free estimate that knows no spacing: a label the spacing widens past its box then ends in an ellipsis and is never cut through a letter, and its whole text stays in the accessible name (tested on the demo, horizontal and vertical). Spacing a reader turns on while transitions are switched off is measured at the next resize.

tests.test: [claim:text-spacing] measures labels with the reader's text spacing

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.remarks: The tooltip shows on hover and on keyboard focus, the pointer can move onto it and it stays, it does not time out, and Escape dismisses it and nothing else.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.remarks: Every gesture has a key, and a parity test holds each key to the command the gesture gives: pan, zoom, select, move, resize, change lane, add, remove, groups, time bars, the overview strip, range selection, the task grid.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.remarks: The timeline is one focus stop; Tab and Shift+Tab leave it, Escape lets go of the focus and the selection, and keys it does not use stay the page's.

tests.test: is one focus stop, a listbox named and oriented for the reader
Esc releases the focus and the selection
the other keys stay with the page

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.remarks: Single-character keys (`+`, `-`, `g`, `n`, `r`, `[`, `]`) act only while the timeline has the focus; the host can replace the whole key table or switch the keys off with the gestures.

tests.test: takes a table of the host's own
is off when the host says so
leaves ctrl and meta to the browser

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.remarks: Nothing times out: the tooltip stays until it is dismissed, and nothing the library draws has a deadline.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.remarks: Rolling mode, the one thing that moves on its own, stops as soon as the reader pans or zooms, and resumes only on `follow()`; transitions are short and arrive in one frame under reduced motion.

tests.test: keeps now in the view, lets go when the reader pans

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.remarks: Nothing flashes: a zoom draws on every frame each label shown before it and after it, so no label blinks.

tests.test: shows on every frame of a zoom each label shown before it and after it

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion. The timeline is one focus stop, so it adds no block to bypass.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion; the page is the host's.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.remarks: One focus stop, entered with Tab; inside it the arrows move in reading order. The date prompt for `g` is the host's: the demo's hands the focus back where it was, and the timeline keeps its focused item.

tests.test: Tab onto the timeline, every item by arrow keys, the focus is visible
g, date, Enter: the view jumps there, and the focus returns

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.remarks: The library draws no links; a link in a template is the host's.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.remarks: A site-level criterion.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.remarks: The listbox has the accessible name the host gives it; every button and word the library draws comes from the dictionary, so a host's language reaches all of them.

tests.test: is one focus stop, a listbox named and oriented for the reader

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.remarks: The focused item is drawn with a ring that meets 3:1, in both themes, and the ring moves with the arrows. The timeline's own outline is drawn inside its box, so a container with `overflow: hidden` does not cut it: every pixel of the four edges of a clipping card exactly the timeline's size is the outline's colour, and none is when the same outline is drawn outside (the control). In forced colours the ring and the outline take the reader's `Highlight`, the ring 3 pixels wide.

tests.test: the focus outline is drawn inside the timeline
paint in the reader's system colours, wider where selected

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: An item the keyboard moves to is brought into view with a margin, across the lanes too, so the focus is not hidden at an edge; at 320 pixels the element brings every item wholly into view. The bottom sheet the library opens over a narrow screen leaves the focused item in view, and the focus on the timeline (tested at 320 pixels, for every item).

tests.test: brings an off-screen item into view, keeping a margin
scrolls the lanes to an item across, both ways
the bottom sheet never hides the focused item

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.remarks: Pinch and two-finger tap have single-pointer twins: a double tap zooms in, and zoom presets (`zoomPresets`) zoom out with one tap. Panning without a path takes the wheel or the keys; a one-tap pan control is not built in.

tests.test: zooms in on a double tap, about the tapped point
gives every gesture a programmatic twin

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.remarks: A gesture ends on pointer cancel without acting, a drag is not an edit until it passes its threshold, and every edit is one command that undo takes back exactly.

tests.test: ends the gesture on pointercancel and stops panning
undo restores the starting state EXACTLY

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.remarks: An item's accessible name starts with the label it shows.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.remarks: Nothing is operated by moving the device.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.remarks: Every drag has a keyboard twin (Alt and an arrow moves, Shift and an arrow resizes, the arrows move a time bar), and zooming has buttons. Moving or resizing an item with single pointer taps, without dragging, is not built in.

tests.test: to the command a drag gives

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: Under touch, an item is hit from beyond its edges, and the dense layout raises even a mouse's target to 24 CSS pixels. In the comfortable and compact layouts a mouse target can be smaller than 24 pixels where items are short and close together.

tests.test: dense raises even a mouse's target to 24 px
a finger reaches a 2 px item it misses by 10 px along time

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion; the page's language is the host's.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.remarks: The words the library says are the host's dictionary, in the page's language; the labels are the host's data.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.remarks: Focus changes nothing but the focus: it shows the tooltip and rings the item, and opens nothing, loads nothing and moves nowhere else.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.remarks: `g` only asks the host for a date (`jumpRequest`); the view changes when the host calls `scrollTo` with the date the reader confirmed, never on input alone.

tests.test: asks the host for a date on g, and goTo centres it

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.remarks: A site-level criterion.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.remarks: The same function is called the same everywhere: every word comes from one dictionary, and the views say what the core says.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.remarks: A site-level criterion.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.remarks: A window that fails to load is marked on the axis, and the page stays free of accessibility errors; a move the host refuses (`canMove`) puts the item back without a message of the library's own — the host says why.

tests.test: the async page with failed windows

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.remarks: The library draws no form field: the date prompt for `g` is the host's, and so are its label and instructions (the demo's is labelled, and passes axe with the prompt open).

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.remarks: The library takes no typed input: the date prompt for `g` is the host's, and so is what it says about a date it cannot read.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.remarks: The library saves nothing: every edit is one command with its own inverse, and undoing it restores the start exactly.

tests.test: undo restores the starting state EXACTLY

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.remarks: The library asks for nothing twice; it has no multi-step process.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: The library has no authentication.

criteria.name: Parsing (Obsolete and removed)
criteria.remarks: Obsolete and removed in WCAG 2.2; for HTML it is always satisfied.

earlier.remarks: EN 301 549 and the Revised Section 508 take this criterion from WCAG 2.1 and 2.0, whose errata hold it always satisfied for content in HTML or XML; the timeline is SVG, an XML language, in HTML.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.remarks: Every item has its role (`option`), name, state (`aria-selected`) and place; the listbox has its name and orientation; axe finds no violation on the demo, its variants and every documentation page with a live example.

tests.test: makes every drawn item an option with a unique id
the demo in its initial state

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.remarks: Changes the reader did not cause by focus are announced politely: the calendar's period, the tools' announcements, through a polite live region.

tests.test: the period keys and the buttons page the same way, and say so

evaluation: Automated tests in a real browser (Chromium, through Playwright): axe-core with the WCAG 2.2 A and AA rules on every state of the demo pages and on every page and live example of this site, on a desktop and a phone viewport, with a negative control that proves the scan sees.

Measurements a scan cannot make, in the same browser: reflow at 320 CSS pixels and 256 pixels tall, page zoom at 200%, text-only enlargement, WCAG's text-spacing override, forced colours in a light and a dark palette, and the focus outline in a container that clips — each by its boxes, computed styles or pixels.

Unit tests of the engine (Vitest): the accessible names, roles and states of every item, the keyboard order and every key, the parity of each key with its gesture, contrast of every colour pair in both themes, computed as WCAG defines it.
Every criterion marked Supports cites at least one of these tests, and the release check runs every cited test and fails if one is not green.

**No manual test with a screen reader has been done yet**, nor any review by a person with a disability: what a screen reader announces rests on the roles, names and states the tests check, not on listening to one. Only Chromium has been tested.

en301549.title: Functional Performance Statements
en301549.remarks: Not assessed on their own: where they apply to web content they are met through the WCAG criteria of chapter 9. Without a manual test with a screen reader, usage without vision (4.2.1) rests on the automated checks of names, roles and states.

en301549.title: Generic Requirements
en301549.remarks: Closed functionality, the activation of accessibility features, biometrics, preserving accessibility through conversion, operable parts and locking keys (5.1–5.8) belong to devices and closed systems; a web component has none. Simultaneous user actions (5.9): the one gesture that takes two fingers, pinch, has single keys (`+` and `-`), see 2.1.1.

en301549.title: ICT with Two-Way Voice Communication
en301549.remarks: The library has no voice communication.

en301549.title: Web
en301549.remarks: Chapter 9 is WCAG 2.1 levels A and AA: clause 9.x.y.z is success criterion x.y.z, and each row of the WCAG tables above names its clause.

en301549.title: Non-web Documents
en301549.remarks: The timeline is not a document. The export plugin, outside this report's scope, writes pictures of the view as SVG, PNG or PDF; they are not evaluated.

en301549.title: Software
en301549.remarks: The library is web content that runs in a browser, evaluated under chapter 9. It is not an authoring tool (11.8): editing moves and resizes items, it does not author content for others.

en301549.title: Documentation and Support Services
en301549.remarks: Product documentation (12.1): the accessibility guide documents the keys, what a screen reader gets, motion, contrast and forced colours; this documentation site is scanned by axe at WCAG 2.2 AA on every page, with 0 violations, but has not been reviewed by hand. Support services (12.2): not applicable — there is no support service, only the public issue tracker.

en301549.title: ICT Providing Relay or Emergency Service Access
en301549.remarks: The library provides no relay or emergency service.

section508.title: Functional Performance Criteria
section508.remarks: Not assessed on their own: where they apply to web content they are met through the WCAG criteria (E205.4). Without a manual test with a screen reader, use without vision (302.1) rests on the automated checks of names, roles and states.

section508.title: Software
section508.remarks: The library is web content that runs in a browser, held to WCAG 2.0 levels A and AA through E205.4 (the WCAG tables above); it reaches assistive technology through the browser's accessibility tree (see 4.1.2). User preferences (503.2) exempt software that runs in a web browser; the timeline follows forced colours and reduced motion even so. It is not an authoring tool (504).

section508.title: Support Documentation and Services
section508.remarks: The accessibility guide documents the keys, what a screen reader gets, motion, contrast and forced colours (602.2); this documentation site is scanned by axe at WCAG 2.2 AA on every page, with 0 violations, but has not been reviewed by hand (602.3). There is no support service (603), only the public issue tracker.

section508.title: Electronic Content
section508.remarks: Electronic content is WCAG 2.0 levels A and AA (E205.4, through 501 for web): the WCAG tables above, minus the criteria WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 added — each row says whether it applies.
